summary: Ran step M2-S04 of .sfskills/builds/case-onboarding (plan v5, status building). The step was in build_plan.py next, its step:M2-S04 gate was already approved, and it was claimed pending -> running before any agent work. Owning agent metadata-builder was executed inline per its AGENT.md and wrote 9 files under artefacts/M2-S04/ - three Queues, three Groups, package.xml, the queue-retirement runbook and deploy-order.md. check-outputs returned ok, the step's declared checker exits 0, both envelopes validate, and the step was set built. Terminal status: built.
confidence_rationale: Step 9 MEDIUM on the second row: an optional input of the owning agent had no value in the plan and the agent defaulted it - plan.json carries no api_version key, so metadata-builder applied its documented 62.0 default (which matches every prior step's package.xml). Everything on the HIGH row holds: M2-S04 was in next, every required input of the owning agent resolved from the plan, both envelopes validate against output-envelope.schema.json, check-outputs exited 0, no undeclared artefact appeared, and no file was written outside artefacts/M2-S04/ and this agent's own envelopes/M2-S04/ directory. Not LOW: nothing is missing, empty or malformed and the step is not blocked.

The step therefore stands at built, not tested.

process_observations.observation: build_plan.py next, set-status running and check-outputs each did their own gate work, so the runner never had to re-derive runnability or adjudicate the outputs by eye.

The 2026-09-12 amend-step that added deploy-order.md to outputs[] worked as intended: the file the owning agent writes on every run is now a declared path check-outputs confirms, so this is the first step in the build where nothing is produced undeclared.
The concurrent M2-S03 run was visible in plan.json as running throughout and neither its status nor its artefacts directory was touched by this invocation.

The step's acceptance_tests[0] description predicts one checker WARN and names it, but the built artefacts produce two, because the Tier 2 queue mailbox address the fixture assumed is not answered anywhere in the plan.

M2-S04 declares depends_on M2-S02 but nothing it writes can reference a permission set or permission set group, so the dependency is a sequencing preference rather than a metadata one - worth knowing before anyone reads the absence of PSG names as a missing link.

A cited skill's checker (check_data_skew_and_sharing_performance.py) exits 1 on three INFO findings that no change inside this step's declared outputs can clear; the owning agent stated the disagreement and did not edit the checker, and this runner did not convert it into a failed step because that checker is not one of the step's declared acceptance tests.

This agent's Wave 10 persistence clause names a docs/reports/build-step-runner/ pair, and the caller's instruction for this run forbids writing outside the build directory; the build-scoped envelope pair was written and the repo-scoped pair was not, which matches what all four earlier steps of this build did.
The step is built and its seven declared acceptance tests have not been adjudicated.
